A model is fitted to say something the data do not show directly: the time course of a species
nobody measured, or the response to an experiment nobody did. How certain such a prediction is
follows from the uncertainty of the parameters, but not in a simple way: the parameters enter
nonlinearly, and some of them, the totals and the scales, are only determined in combination.
The prediction profile likelihood (Kreutz et al. 2012, BMC Syst Biol 6:120) answers the question
directly, without the detour over parameter intervals. This chapter computes the band of nuclear
IκBα after TNFα in the reduced model of [chapter 5](guide-profiles.html). Nuclear IκBα is not
measured; in the publication it decides when NFκB leaves the nucleus again (Oppelt et al. 2018,
Fig. 5). The code is `prediction.R`.

## Prediction profile

A prediction $z = h(t, \theta)$, here the concentration of nuclear IκBα at time $t$, is a function of
the parameters. Its profile is the objective minimised over all parameters that predict $z$:

$$\mathrm{PPL}(z) = \min_{\theta \,:\, h(t, \theta) = z} \; -2 \log L(\theta) .$$

As for a parameter, the values $z$ with $\mathrm{PPL}(z) - \min \mathrm{PPL}$ below the $1 - \alpha$
quantile of $\chi^2_1$ form a confidence interval of level $1 - \alpha$ for the prediction. The
prediction is one combination of the parameters, so the interval is the projection of the
confidence region of the parameters onto it, and it is as wide as the data leave it, no matter
how many parameters it depends on. A prediction that depends only on combinations the data
determine is narrow even where single parameters are not.

The constraint $h(t, \theta) = z$ is not a parameter that `profile()` could hold fixed. A
validation data point turns it into one: $z$ becomes an additional parameter $v$, and the term

$$\left( \frac{h(t, \theta) - v}{\sigma_v} \right)^2$$

ties the prediction to it. For $\sigma_v \to 0$ the profile of $v$ is the prediction profile; with a
$\sigma_v$ small against the width of the band, the data term along the profile of $v$ is the
prediction profile to within that width. `datapointL2()` builds the term as an `objfn`. It reads
the prediction from the evaluation of `normL2()`, which therefore has to predict at the time $t$,
`times = t`.

The profile of $v$ minimises the data term plus the validation term over $\theta$, and its
threshold applies to that sum, the prior left out as in [chapter 5](guide-profiles.html).
`datapointL2()` reports its value under the attribute `attrName`, `"validation"` by default; with
`attrName = "data"` it adds to the data term of `normL2()`, so that `stop = "data"` in `profile()`
and `confint()` read the sum. Where the model cannot follow $v$, the validation term grows and
ends the profile; with the data term alone, the profile would walk on until its step limit.

## Band

```{r, include = FALSE, eval = predicted}
# the decades of the prediction at the times of the band
decades <- log10(range(readRDS("results/prediction.rds")$band$value))
```

`prediction.R` takes the reduced model at its best fit and computes the prediction profile of
nuclear IκBα in the stimulated condition at 45 times, densest at the flanks of its pulse, in
parallel, with the settings of the profiles of [chapter 5](guide-profiles.html). The predicted
concentration spans `r ifStored(predicted, inWords(floor(diff(decades))))` orders of magnitude over
the time course, so the profiles run on its logarithm, like the parameters: a second observation
function adds `lognIkb` to the readouts, the validation point has the standard deviation 0.01 on the
logarithm, one percent of the concentration, and the interval returns to the concentration by the
exponential. On the concentration itself, $v$ would be as small as
$10^{`r ifStored(predicted, floor(decades[1]))`}$ next to parameters of order one, and the path
equation of the profile would be numerically singular.

```{r predictionsetup, eval = FALSE}
```

`confint()` reads the interval off each profile, from the data term:

```{r predictionband, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = !predicted}
cat("> Results pending: `results/prediction.rds` of the project is written by `prediction.R`.\n")
```

```{r, eval = predicted}
saved <- readRDS("results/prediction.rds")
band <- saved$band
band[band$time %in% c(0, 10, 30, 55, 60, 70, 85, 90, 120, 240, 360), ]
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = predicted}
# the times at which a side of the profile ends below the threshold
short <- band$time[!vapply(saved$profiles, function(pr) {
  d <- as.data.frame(pr)
  min(d$data[c(1, nrow(d))]) - d$data[d$constraint == 0][1] > qchisq(0.95, 1)
}, logical(1))]
if (length(short))
  cat(sprintf(paste("At %s minutes one side ends before the threshold, and `confint()`",
                    "extrapolates the last part of the profile.\n"),
              paste(short, collapse = ", ")))
```

The prediction profiles at three times, drawn by `plotProfile()` like the profiles of parameters
in [chapter 5](guide-profiles.html), from the data term, which holds the validation point; one
panel per time:

```{r, fig.height = 3.5, eval = predicted}
times <- c(10, 70, 240)
shown <- setNames(saved$profiles[match(times, band$time)], paste(times, "min"))
plotProfile(shown, mode == "data") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~proflist, scales = "free_x") +
  ggplot2::guides(colour = "none") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "log nuclear IκBα [total NFκB]")
```

The band over time, around the prediction of the best fit:

```{r, eval = predicted}
controls(gReduced, name = "attachInput") <- TRUE
bestReduced <- as.parvec(readRDS("results/reduced.rds")$fits)
times <- seq(0, 360, length.out = 361)
course <- data.frame(time = times,
                     value = prdReduced(times, c(bestReduced, gaugeReduced), deriv = FALSE)$TNF[, "nIkb"])
ggplot2::ggplot(course, ggplot2::aes(time, value)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(data = band, ggplot2::aes(x = time, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                       inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = band, ggplot2::aes(y = lower), shape = 4) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = band, ggplot2::aes(y = upper), shape = 4) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 360, 60)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "time [min]", y = "nuclear IκBα [total NFκB]") +
  theme_dMod()
```

The concentration is in units of the total of NFκB, the unit the gauge of
[chapter 2](guide-symmetries.html) sets; a prediction of an absolute concentration would need a
measurement of one.
